mainTopic: Whether owning the use of something counts as owning it, and רבי אליעזר's rule that 'his' means 'only his'; then a new משנה on fixed payments for humiliating blows.
overview: The amud opens by finishing the discussion of a wife's slave whom she injures. One explanation uses רבא's rule that שחרור cancels a שעבוד. The גמרא asks whether this makes רבא's rule a dispute between תנאים, and it gives two answers. The first answer says חכמים made a husband's lien extra strong. The second says the real argument is whether קנין פירות כקנין הגוף דמי. That question is tied to a ברייתא about a slave sold on condition that he serve the seller for thirty days, where four תנאים argue about who gets the exemption of יום או יומים. רבא explains that רבי אליעזר reads כספו as 'only his', so neither owner is exempt. The גמרא then uses this idea to explain אמימר's ruling on selling נכסי מלוג, and a ברייתא that a half-slave or a partners' slave does not go free through injury to his limbs. Finally, a new משנה begins, listing fixed payments for insulting acts, from a plain blow up to a backhand slap and other public humiliations.

steps.title: Three things that cancel a lien
steps.stepSummary: רבא's rule is that הקדש, חמץ and שחרור cancel any שעבוד on an item. This rule explains why the slave goes free even though the husband has rights to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Consecrating to the Temple, חמץ becoming forbidden, and freeing a slave all cancel any lien on the item.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes an explanation by quoting רבא's rule. Freeing a slave wipes out any lien on him, so the husband's rights do not stop the slave from going free.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wife owns the slave and the husband only has a lien, meaning a right to the slave's work. According to רבא, שחרור is strong enough to break that lien. So when the wife knocks out the slave's tooth, he goes free and the husband's rights disappear.

keyTerms.meaning: Dedicating something to the Temple
Leavened food, which becomes forbidden on פסח
Freeing a slave
Cancel, uproot
A lien, a claim someone has on an item

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the anchor for the rest of this section. The next steps ask whether all the תנאים accept it.

phrases.english: Consecration, chametz, and freeing a slave
phrases.notes: חמץ here means the moment פסח arrives and the chametz becomes forbidden.

phrases.english: cancel out of the hands of a lien.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֶקְדֵּשׁ, חָמֵץ וְשִׁחְרוּר מַפְקִיעִים מִידֵי שִׁיעְבּוּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation from the previous daf of the ברייתא that says the slave goes free.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Freeing a slave, like הקדש and חמץ, cancels any existing lien.

steps.title: Is רבא's rule a dispute between תנאים?
steps.stepSummary: If the 'goes free' ברייתא follows רבא, then the 'does not go free' ברייתא seems to reject רבא. That would make רבא's rule a matter of תנאים dispute.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that רבא's rule is a dispute between תנאים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the explanation from step 1. If one ברייתא agrees with רבא, the other ברייתא seems to argue on him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמורא's rule is weaker if a תנא disagrees with it. The גמרא prefers an explanation in which רבא's rule is accepted by everyone. So it asks whether this explanation forces us to say תנאים argued about רבא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say?, which opens a suggestion the גמרא would rather avoid
תנאים, the sages of the משנה era

phrases.english: Shall we say that Rava's rule is a dispute of Tannaim?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation built on רבא's rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the two ברייתות split over רבא's rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If one ברייתא depends on רבא's rule, the opposing ברייתא must reject it. That would make רבא's rule a dispute between תנאים.

steps.title: Everyone agrees with רבא, but the husband's lien is stronger
steps.stepSummary: Everyone accepts רבא's rule. The ברייתא that keeps the slave a slave holds that חכמים made a husband's lien on his wife's property extra strong, so freeing the slave cannot cancel it.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone holds like רבא. But here the Rabbis made the husband's lien strong.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that nobody argues with רבא. The 'does not go free' ברייתא simply holds that a husband's lien is a special, extra-strong lien.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually שחרור cancels a lien. But חכמים strengthened a husband's rights in his wife's property, so this lien is an exception that שחרור cannot break. The two ברייתות then disagree only about this special lien, not about רבא's general rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
The Rabbis made it strong
Husband

phrases.aramaic: לָא; דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ דְּרָבָא,
phrases.english: No; everyone holds the rule of Rava,
and here the Rabbis strengthened
the lien of the husband.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא; דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא אִית לְהוּ דְּרָבָא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the dispute to a special case, so the general rule stays agreed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות argue about whether שחרור cancels a lien at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: All agree שחרור cancels a lien. They argue only about whether the husband's specially strengthened lien is an exception.

steps.title: Another answer: they argue whether owning the use is like owning the item
steps.stepSummary: A second answer. Both ברייתות reject תקנת אושא. Their real argument is whether קנין פירות כקנין הגוף דמי, meaning whether owning the rights to the use counts as owning the item itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: everyone agrees that these תנאים do not hold of תקנת אושא. Here they argue whether owning the produce is like owning the item itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different way to explain the two ברייתות that does not involve רבא's rule at all. The question is whether the husband, who owns the slave's work, counts as an owner of the slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If owning the use counts as ownership, then the husband is also an owner, and the wife's blow alone cannot free the slave. If owning the use does not count, then the wife is the only owner, and her blow frees him. Because both sides reject תקנת אושא, the husband's strengthened rights play no part in this answer.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say, which introduces a second answer
A rabbinic decree made in אושא that strengthened a husband's rights in his wife's property
Owning the rights to use something and its produce
Owning the item itself
They disagree about

steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not say רבא's rule is wrong. It simply explains the two ברייתות a different way, so רבא's rule never comes up.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say: everyone agrees

phrases.aramaic: לֵית לְהוּ לְהָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי תַּקָּנַת אוּשָׁא,
phrases.english: that these Tannaim do not hold of the Usha decree,
phrases.notes: This decree is what made the husband's hold on the property extra strong, so this answer drops step 3's reason.

phrases.english: and here, about whether ownership of the produce
is like ownership of the item itself, they disagree.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לֵית לְהוּ לְהָנֵי תַּנָּאֵי תַּקָּנַת אוּשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the challenge in step 2, replacing the reason given in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the dispute to a different underlying principle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתות argue about cancelling a lien through שחרור.
steps.terutzMaskana: They argue whether קנין פירות counts as קנין הגוף, which decides whether the husband is a co-owner.

steps.title: Linking the argument to an older Tannaitic dispute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the question of קנין פירות is already argued by תנאים, in a ברייתא about selling a slave on condition that he serve the seller for thirty days first.
steps.simpleTranslation: This matches the dispute of these תנאים, as taught in a ברייתא: One who sells his slave to another and arranges with him that the slave will serve him for thirty days...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins quoting a ברייתא to show where the קנין פירות question is already debated. This step is a setup, and the actual dispute comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case, for thirty days the seller has the slave's work while the buyer owns the slave himself. This is the same split as husband and wife: one side owns the use and the other owns the item. So the dispute about who counts as the owner here will mirror the dispute in step 4.

keyTerms.meaning: A dispute
As it was taught in a ברייתא
He arranged with him, made a deal
On condition that

phrases.english: And it is in the dispute of these Tannaim, as it was taught:
One who sells his slave to another,
and arranged with him on condition
that the slave will serve him for thirty days;
phrases.notes: For those thirty days the seller gets the slave's work, while the buyer already owns the slave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Grounds the second answer in step 4 in an existing dispute between תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: That whether קנין פירות כקנין הגוף דמי is a known dispute between תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about a slave sold on condition that he serve the seller for thirty days

steps.title: רבי מאיר: the seller is the owner because he has the slave's work
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says the first owner, the seller, gets the exemption of יום או יומים, because the slave works for him. The גמרא explains that he holds קנין פירות כקנין הגוף דמי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: the first owner is included in the law of 'a day or two,' because the slave is under him. The גמרא explains: he holds that owning the use of something is like owning the thing itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the first opinion in the ברייתא from Step 5. It then explains that רבי מאיר holds that having the right to use something counts as owning it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During the thirty days, the seller has only the slave's work, and the buyer owns the slave himself. רבי מאיר treats the seller as the real master for the law of יום או יומים. That only makes sense if having the use (קנין פירות) counts like owning the slave (קנין הגוף).

keyTerms.meaning: The first owner, meaning the seller, who keeps the slave's work for thirty days
'A day or two': if a hit slave lives this long before dying, his master is not put to death
'Under him': the slave works for him and is in his service
'He holds': the גמרא is explaining the reason behind an opinion
Owning the use of an item counts like owning the item itself

steps.confusionAlert: Being 'included in the law of a day or two' is a good thing for the master. It means he is NOT put to death if the slave lingers a day or two and then dies.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:

phrases.aramaic: רִאשׁוֹן יֶשְׁנוֹ בְּדִין יוֹם אוֹ יוֹמַיִם,
phrases.english: the first owner is included in the law of 'a day or two days,'
phrases.notes: שמות 21:21. If a master hits his slave and the slave lives a day or two before dying, the master is not put to death.

phrases.english: because the slave is under him.
He holds:
owning the use of something is like owning the thing itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: רִאשׁוֹן יֶשְׁנוֹ בְּדִין יוֹם אוֹ יוֹמַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first opinion in the ברייתא brought in Step 5 and links it to קנין פירות.
steps.raayaObject: That the question of whether קנין פירות כקנין הגוף דמי is a dispute among תנאים (Step 4).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the slave sold on condition that he serve the seller for thirty days. Here, רבי מאיר's ruling for the first owner.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the buyer is the owner because the slave is his property
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the second owner, the buyer, gets the exemption, because the slave is his money. The גמרא explains that he holds קנין פירות is not like קנין הגוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: the second owner is included in the law of 'a day or two,' because the slave is his money. The גמרא explains: he holds that owning the use of something is not like owning the thing itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the second opinion in the ברייתא, which is the opposite of רבי מאיר. It explains that רבי יהודה holds that having only the use does not make you the owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק gives the reason for the exemption as כי כספו הוא, 'because he is his money.' רבי יהודה reads this as being about real ownership of the slave, which the buyer has. Now we see two תנאים taking opposite sides on קנין פירות, and that is exactly the ראיה the גמרא wanted.

keyTerms.meaning: The second owner, meaning the buyer, who owns the slave himself
'His money': the slave is his property (from שמות 21:21)
Not

steps.whyThisMatters: Together with Step 6, this shows a clear dispute between תנאים on קנין פירות. That supports the second answer in Step 4 for why the two ברייתות about the freed slave disagree.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: שֵׁנִי יֶשְׁנוֹ בְּדִין יוֹם אוֹ יוֹמַיִם,
phrases.english: the second owner is included in the law of 'a day or two days,'
because the slave is his money.
phrases.notes: This uses the words of the פסוק itself, כי כספו הוא, 'for he is his money.'

phrases.english: He holds:

phrases.aramaic: קִנְיַן פֵּירוֹת – לָאו כְּקִנְיַן הַגּוּף דָּמֵי.
phrases.english: owning the use of something is not like owning the thing itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: שֵׁנִי יֶשְׁנוֹ בְּדִין יוֹם אוֹ יוֹמַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite opinion to רבי מאיר, which completes the dispute about קנין פירות.
steps.raayaObject: That תנאים argue whether קנין פירות כקנין הגוף דמי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה's ruling in the same ברייתא, that the second owner is the master for this law.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: both are exempt because the question is unsure
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says both owners get the exemption. The גמרא explains that he is unsure whether קנין פירות counts as ownership, and in a doubt about a death penalty we are lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: both of them are included in the law of 'a day or two.' This one because the slave is under him, and that one because the slave is his money. The גמרא explains: he is unsure whether owning the use is like owning the thing or not, and when there is a doubt about a life, we are lenient.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third opinion, that neither owner is put to death. It explains that רבי יוסי is in doubt about קנין פירות, so he is lenient for both of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If קנין פירות counts as ownership, the seller is the master and is exempt. If it does not, the buyer is the master and is exempt. Since רבי יוסי cannot decide, each owner might be the master, and the rule of ספק נפשות להקל means we do not put either one to death.

keyTerms.meaning: Both of them, meaning the seller and the buyer
He is in doubt; he cannot decide
When there is a doubt in a case of life and death, we rule leniently

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי does not hold that both are full owners. He simply does not know which one is the owner, so he is lenient for both.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵיהֶם יֶשְׁנָן בְּדִין יוֹם אוֹ יוֹמַיִם;
phrases.english: both of them are included in the law of 'a day or two days';
this one because the slave is under him,
and that one because the slave is his money.
He is unsure about owning the use of something:
whether it is like owning the thing itself
or whether it is not like owning the thing itself,
and a doubt about lives is ruled leniently.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: שְׁנֵיהֶם יֶשְׁנָן בְּדִין יוֹם אוֹ יוֹמַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third position that is built on the same question of קנין פירות, but leaves it undecided.
steps.raayaObject: That the status of קנין פירות was an open question among תנאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוסי's ruling in the ברייתא, which the גמרא explains as a doubt about קנין פירות.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: neither owner gets the exemption
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says neither owner gets the exemption of יום או יומים. The buyer lacks the slave's work, and the seller lacks ownership of the slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: both of them are not included in the law of 'a day or two.' This one because the slave is not under him, and that one because the slave is not his money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the last opinion in the ברייתא. Here the גמרא does not explain his reasoning, which sets up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר seems to require both things for the exemption: the slave must work for you (תחתיו) and be your property (כספו). During the thirty days, each owner has only one of these, so neither is exempt. Unlike the other three opinions, he is not tied here to one side of קנין פירות.

keyTerms.meaning: They are not (included)
Because he is not

steps.whatToRemember: Four תנאים: רבי מאיר says the seller is exempt (קנין פירות counts). רבי יהודה says the buyer is exempt (it does not count). רבי יוסי says both are exempt (doubt, so lenient). רבי אליעזר says neither is exempt (each has only half of what is needed).

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵיהֶם אֵינָן בְּדִין יוֹם אוֹ יוֹמַיִם;
phrases.english: both of them are not included in the law of 'a day or two days';
this one because the slave is not under him,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the buyer, who does not get the slave's work during the thirty days.

phrases.english: and that one because the slave is not his money.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: שְׁנֵיהֶם אֵינָן בְּדִין יוֹם אוֹ יוֹמַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the list of opinions in the ברייתא with a fourth position that is stricter than all the others.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Neither the seller nor the buyer gets the exemption of יום או יומים during the thirty days, because the exemption needs both the use of the slave and ownership of him.

steps.title: רבא gives the source for רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that רבי אליעזר learns from 'כי כספו הוא' that the slave must be 'his money' alone, belonging only to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What is רבי אליעזר's reason? The verse says 'for he is his money.' That means his money that belongs only to him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the פסוק that רבי אליעזר's opinion from Step 9 is built on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word כספו ('his money') is read as 'money that belongs only to him.' A slave counts only when one owner has both the body and the work. If ownership is split between a seller and a buyer, neither one gets the exemption of יום או יומים.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
'For he is his money' (שמות 21:21)
That belongs only to him, completely his

steps.whyThisMatters: This reading of 'his' as 'only his' is the tool the rest of this section uses to explain other rulings.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר?
phrases.english: Rava said: What is the reason of Rabbi Eliezer?
The verse says: 'For he is his money'
His money that belongs only to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind רבי אליעזר's view from Step 9
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'כספו' means a slave owned completely by one master, both body and work.

steps.title: Whose view does אמימר follow on selling נכסי מלוג?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא matches אמימר's ruling that a sale of נכסי מלוג by the husband or the wife does nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion matches what אמימר said: if a man or a woman sold נכסי מלוג, they did nothing at all?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling of אמימר and asks whose opinion it follows. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In נכסי מלוג the wife owns the property itself, and the husband gets its produce. So each one holds only part of the ownership. אמימר rules that a sale by either of them does not work, and the גמרא wants to know which view stands behind that.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion does this follow?
The wife's property: she owns it, the husband gets its produce
They did nothing at all; the sale does not work

phrases.english: Whose view does this follow, which Ameimar said:
A man or a woman who sold usufruct property
phrases.notes: He means a husband or his wife selling her property: she owns it, but he gets to eat what it produces.

phrases.english: They did not do anything?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי אליעזר's idea of full ownership to find who stands behind a later ruling
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view stands behind אמימר's ruling

steps.title: אמימר follows רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that אמימר follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that אמימר's ruling follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר holds that a person who has only the body or only the produce is not a real owner. The husband has only the produce, and the wife has only the body. So neither one can sell the property alone.

keyTerms.meaning: According to רבי אליעזר

phrases.english: Like whom? Like Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אמימר follows רבי אליעזר: only someone with both the body and the produce counts as an owner.

steps.title: Who taught the ברייתא about a half-slave and a partners' slave?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who taught the ברייתא that a half-slave, or a slave of two partners, does not go free through injury to his ראשי אברים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who taught what the Rabbis taught: one who is half slave and half free, and also a slave of two partners, do not go free through injury to limbs that do not grow back?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא and asks which תנא taught it. This sets up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a slave goes free if his master knocks out his eye or tooth, or destroys one of his ראשי אברים, such as a finger, toe or ear. This ברייתא says the rule does not apply when the slave is not fully owned by one master. The גמרא wants to know whose view that is.

keyTerms.meaning: Who taught this?
Half slave and half free
Partners
Limbs that stick out of the body, like fingers, toes and ears

phrases.english: Who taught that which the Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶּן חוֹרִין,
phrases.english: One who is half slave and half free man,
And likewise a slave of two partners

phrases.aramaic: אֵין יוֹצְאִין בְּרָאשֵׁי אֵבָרִים שֶׁאֵינָן חוֹזְרִין?
phrases.english: Do not go free through limbs that do not grow back?
phrases.notes: This is the rule that a slave goes free when his master knocks out his eye, his tooth, or another limb that can't grow back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second ruling the גמרא will tie to רבי אליעזר
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that a slave who is not fully owned does not go free through injury to his limbs

steps.title: רב מרדכי, quoting רבא: it is רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: רב מרדכי tells רב אשי that, in the name of רבא, the ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרדכי said to רב אשי: This is what they say in רבא's name: it is רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרדכי answers the question by quoting רבא: the ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This step gives only the answer. The reason comes in the next step, where the גמרא shows how רבי אליעזר's reading of the פסוק applies here too.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what they say in רבא's name

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב מָרְדֳּכַי לְרַב אָשֵׁי,
phrases.english: Rav Mordechai said to Rav Ashi,
So they say in the name of Rava:
It is Rabbi Eliezer

steps.title: 'His slave' also means a slave only he owns
steps.stepSummary: Just as 'כספו' means money belonging only to him, 'עבדו' in the פסוק about freeing a slave means a slave belonging only to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Didn't רבי אליעזר say that 'his money' means only his? Here too, 'his slave' means only his.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the ברייתא fits רבי אליעזר. He reads the word 'his' in the same way in both פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about a slave going free says 'עין עבדו', the eye of his slave. Using רבי אליעזר's reading, 'his slave' means a slave owned entirely by this one master. A half-free slave, or a slave shared by partners, is not fully 'his', so he does not go free.

keyTerms.meaning: Didn't he say? (pointing to a known statement)
Here too
'His slave' (שמות 21:26)

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי אליעזר, the word 'his' in the פסוקים about a slave means 'fully and only his.' That explains why he denies the exemption of יום או יומים to split owners, why a split sale of נכסי מלוג does nothing, and why a shared slave does not go free through injury to his limbs.

phrases.english: Didn't Rabbi Eliezer say:
'His money' means that which belongs only to him?
Here too, 'his slave' means that which belongs only to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the answer in Step 14
steps.raayaObject: That the ברייתא about a half-slave and a partners' slave follows רבי אליעזר
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אליעזר's reading of 'כספו' as 'only his', applied to 'עבדו'

steps.title: The basic blow: one סלע, or one מנה according to רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens a new topic. One who strikes his fellow pays a סלע. רבי יהודה, quoting רבי יוסי הגלילי, says he pays a מנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone who hits another person must pay him a סלע. רבי יהודה says in the name of רבי יוסי הגלילי: he must pay a מנה (one hundred זוז).
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with the first and mildest case on its list: a plain blow to another person. There is a disagreement about how much he must pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא sets the payment at a סלע, a small amount. רבי יהודה, quoting רבי יוסי הגלילי, sets it much higher, at a מנה. Both agree there is a fixed amount; they only argue about how big it is.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה, the base text the גמרא will discuss
One who strikes or hits another person
A coin worth four זוז
A sum of one hundred זוז

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who strikes his fellow
gives him a sela.
phrases.notes: A סלע is four זוז. Keep that in mind, because the amounts climb steeply from here.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says in the name of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili:
a maneh.
phrases.notes: A מנה is one hundred זוז, twenty-five times more than a סלע.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַתּוֹקֵעַ לַחֲבֵירוֹ נוֹתֵן לוֹ סֶלַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a brand-new משנה. It does not connect to the earlier discussion of אמימר and רבי אליעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who strikes his fellow pays a סלע; רבי יהודה in the name of רבי יוסי הגלילי says a מנה.

steps.title: A slap costs 200 זוז, and a backhand slap costs 400
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues with more insulting blows. A slap on the cheek costs 200 זוז, and a slap with the back of the hand costs 400 זוז.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he slapped him, he gives him two hundred זוז. If he slapped him with the back of his hand, he gives him four hundred זוז.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps moving up its list to more insulting kinds of hitting, and the payment goes up each time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A slap is more insulting than a plain blow, so it costs more. A backhand slap is even more insulting, so the amount doubles again. The physical hurt is not what drives the price up; the level of disrespect is.

keyTerms.meaning: He slapped him on the cheek
With the back of his hand
A silver coin, the basic unit used for these payments

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume the bigger payment means a worse injury. A backhand slap may hurt less than a regular slap, yet it costs double because it is more insulting.

phrases.english: If he slapped him,
he gives him two hundred zuz.
If with the back of his hand,
he gives him four hundred zuz.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same list from the previous step, moving to more insulting blows with higher payments.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A slap costs 200 זוז; a backhand slap costs 400 זוז.

steps.title: Other shameful acts that also cost 400 זוז
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists more acts that each cost 400 זוז: pulling an ear, pulling out hair, spitting that reaches the person, taking off his cloak, and uncovering a woman's head in the marketplace.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he pulled his ear, pulled out his hair, spat and his spit reached him, took his cloak off him, or uncovered a woman's head in the marketplace, he pays four hundred זוז.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists a group of shameful acts, and they all get the same top payment of 400 זוז.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most of these acts cause little or no physical harm. Spitting or taking off a cloak may not hurt at all. They still get the highest fixed payment, which shows the משנה is pricing the humiliation, not the injury.

keyTerms.meaning: He pulled (or yanked) his ear
He pulled out his hair
He spat
His cloak, his outer garment
He uncovered a woman's head

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה sets fixed payments that rise with how insulting the act is: a blow (a סלע, or a מנה according to רבי יוסי הגלילי), a slap (200 זוז), and a backhand slap or other public humiliations (400 זוז).
steps.whyThisMatters: This list shows that payment for embarrassment can be owed even when there is no real injury, which sets up the גמרא's discussion that follows.

phrases.english: If he pulled his ear;
pulled out his hair;
spat, and his spittle reached him;
removed his cloak from him;
uncovered the head of a woman in the marketplace –
he gives him four hundred zuz.
phrases.notes: This payment covers every case in the list. In the last case, the woman herself is the one who gets paid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a list of non-hitting shameful acts that get the same 400 זוז payment as the backhand slap.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pulling an ear, pulling out hair, spitting that reaches him, removing his cloak, or uncovering a woman's head in the marketplace each costs 400 זוז.
